analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour + Peter Oppenheimer FOMC Minutes Datacenter Economics Hearing Aids Babcock (I) Tesco 8 Oct 2026
key_insights: US equities closed lower amid a renewed global bond sell-off and defensive rotation: SPX -22bps to 7801, DJIA -66bps to 51179, NDX -22bps to 27538. Only 3 of 11 sectors rose (Utilities +23bps), Industrials fell 170bps.
GS US Cyclicals vs Defensives pair (GSPUCYDE) traded -159bps. Russell underperformed NDX for the 4th straight day and 17 of the last 20 sessions.
In Europe, Banks (SX7E -3.4%) and tech/semis (GSSBSEMI -4.4%) underperformed while Telcos (+1.1%) and Pharma (+1.7%) rose in a defensive rotation.
GS prime book net exposure to Mag7 is near 22% of total US exposure, the highest since the start of 2022, while overall market net positioning is still low.
Semis and semi equipment are ~12% of total US exposure on the GS prime book, down from a June peak of 14% and up from ~6% at the start of the year.
GS prime data shows US Tech had its largest monthly buying in September since Feb 2025 and was the only sector net bought on the prime book that month.

GS expects a second Fed hike in December but sees a strong chance the FOMC concludes further tightening is unnecessary. Most participants in the minutes viewed another increase as likely appropriate by year end, with decisions dependent on incoming information.

Basket idea: GS Consumer Experiences basket (GSXUCEXP) has underperformed SPXXAI despite experiences spending growth accelerating from 1% in Q1 2025 to 6% in Q1 2026 versus 2% for broader services. GS says valuations are attractive, revisions appear close to inflecting and positioning is not crowded.
Peter Oppenheimer chartpack flagged as worth a look, with no content given in the text.

Alberto Gandolfi: Utilities are moving toward a 'DC Infrastructure Services' model providing land, grid access and energy to datacenters. Covered Utilities own c.25 GW of connection points, mostly in Europe, worth c.€20bn on recent transaction values.
GS simulates that Solaria monetizing its grid access could add c.45% to its share price. PPC, Drax, Fortum and RWE also have meaningful exposure to the theme.

Sonova upgraded to Buy, PT raised to CHF315 from CHF230, on Virto R momentum, y/y share gains at Costco following its 2025 re-entry, and an APAC focus. GS expects constant-currency revenue growth at the upper end of FY27 guidance (GSe 7.8% vs consensus +6.6%) and adjusted EBIT growth of +12.6% vs +6.5%.

Babcock initiated at Neutral with a GBP10 PT (15% upside). Defence and nuclear positions and a £9.8bn backlog support medium-term visibility. Civil nuclear is the clearest upside and contract execution is the main downside risk.

Tesco 1H EBIT came in at GBP1.78bn vs consensus GBP1.72bn on a 13bps margin gain. 1H LfL was +1% vs consensus +1.2%. FY guide narrowed to GBP3.15-3.3bn (prior 3.0-3.3bn, consensus 3.25bn), FCF in line, share buyback raised to GBP950m vs consensus GBP750m.

market_movers.rationale: Sonova upgraded to Buy on Virto R momentum, Costco share gains and APAC focus. GSe FY27 constant-currency revenue growth of 7.8% vs consensus 6.6%.
Babcock initiated at Neutral with 15% upside. Backlog of £9.8bn gives visibility, and civil nuclear is the main upside.
Tesco 1H EBIT of GBP1.78bn beat consensus of GBP1.72bn, FY guide narrowed to the upper end, and the buyback was raised to GBP950m.

sector_views.rationale: Utilities with grid connection points could monetize them via datacenter infrastructure services. Covered names own c.25 GW worth c.€20bn.
Basket has lagged despite experiences spending growth of 6% in Q1 2026. Valuations are attractive and positioning is not crowded.
